arxiv-2110-11476.title: Two-loop amplitudes for di-Higgs and di-pseudo-Higgs productions through quark annihilation in QCD
arxiv-2110-11476.creator: Taushif Ahmed a,1 , V. Ravindran b,2 , Aparna Sankar b,3 and Surabhi Tiwari b,4
arxiv-2110-11476.description: Abstract Through this article, we present the two-loop massless QCD corrections to the production of di-Higgs and di-pseudo-Higgs boson through quark annihilation in the large top quark mass limit. Within dimensional regularisation, we employ the non-anticommuting γ 5 \gamma_{5} and treat it under the Larin prescription.

arxiv-2210-12100.title: Boomerang: Local sampling on image manifolds using diffusion models
arxiv-2210-12100.creator: Lorenzo Luzi enzo@rice.edu, Paul M. Mayer pmm3@rice.edu, Josue Casco-Rodriguez jc135@rice.edu, Ali Siahkoohi alisk@rice.edu, Richard G. Baraniuk richb@rice.edu
arxiv-2210-12100.description: Abstract The inference stage of diffusion models can be seen as running a reverse-time diffusion stochastic differential equation, where samples from a Gaussian latent distribution are transformed into samples from a target distribution that usually reside on a low-dimensional manifold, e.g., an image manifold.

arxiv-2310-18024.title: Encounter-based approach to target search problems: a review
arxiv-2310-18024.creator: Denis S. Grebenkov
arxiv-2310-18024.description: Abstract In this review, we present the encounter-based approach to target search problems, in which the diffusive dynamics is described by the joint probability of the position of the particle and the number of its encounters with a given target set.

arxiv-2409-17068.title: Relativistic and Recoil Corrections to Vacuum Polarization in Muonic Systems: Three–Photon Exchange, Gauge Invariance and Numerical Values
arxiv-2409-17068.creator: Gregory S. Adkins, Ulrich D. Jentschura
arxiv-2409-17068.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Gregory S. Adkins, Ulrich D. Jentschura. For an accurate theoretical description of muonic bound systems, it is crucial to consistently treat relativistic and recoil corrections to vacuum polarization. The one-loop vacuum-polarization effect is by far the dominant quantum electrodynamic (QED) energy correction for bound muons, being of order α ​ ( Z ​ α ) 2 ​ m r \alpha(Z\alpha)^{2}m_{r} , where α \alpha is the fine-structure constant, Z Z is the nuclear charge number, and m r m_{r} is the reduced mass.

arxiv-2504-11822.title: Properties of Near Field Focusing for Cylindrical Dipole Arrays in Enclosed Array Volume
arxiv-2504-11822.creator: Jiawang Li
arxiv-2504-11822.description: Abstract Motivated by large intelligent surface applications, the electric field properties of near field focusing using phase conjugation method are analyzed for cylindrical dipole arrays. Firstly, for the transmitting antennas featuring vertical polarization, the polarization characteristic is decomposed along the x x , y y , and z z directions.

arxiv-2506-05054.title: How does picosecond structural deformation of (Ba,Sr)TiO 3 relate to the pyroelectric effect? Journal: Journal of Alloys and Compounds
arxiv-2506-05054.creator: D. Schmidt, J. Wawra, D. Hensel, M. Brede, R. Hühne, P. Gaal
arxiv-2506-05054.description: Abstract The pyroelectric effect in ferroelectric thin films is typically composed of different contributions, which are difficult to disentangle. In addition, clamping to the substrate interface plays an important role. We studied epitaxial (Ba,Sr)TiO 3 thin films grown on NdScO 3 to see if time-resolved measurements can shed more light on the complex interaction.

arxiv-2506-16397.title: New Bounds for the Ideal Proof System in Positive Characteristic
arxiv-2506-16397.creator: Amik Raj Behera, Nutan Limaye, Varun Ramanathan, Srikanth Srinivasan
arxiv-2506-16397.description: Abstract In this work, we prove upper and lower bounds over fields of positive characteristics for several fragments of the Ideal Proof System (IPS), an algebraic proof system introduced by Grochow and Pitassi (J. ACM 2018). Our results extend the works of Forbes, Shpilka, Tzameret, and Wigderson (Theory of Computing 2021) and also of Govindasamy, Hakoniemi, and Tzameret (FOCS 2022).

arxiv-2511-03269.title: A decomposition theorem for the Hochschild homology of symmetric powers of a dg category
arxiv-2511-03269.creator: Ville Nordström
arxiv-2511-03269.description: Abstract We prove a conjecture by Belmans, Fu and Krug concerning the Hochschild homology of the symmetric powers of a small dg category 𝒞 \mathscr{C} . More precisely, we show that these groups decompose into pieces that only depend on the Hochschild homology of the dg category 𝒞 \mathscr{C} .

pmc-10548714.creator: Zahra Zare, Elmira Hajizadeh, Maryam Mahmoodi, Reza Nazari, Leila Shahmoradi, Sorayya Rezayi
pmc-10548714.description: BackgroundObesity is a multifaceted condition that impacts individuals across various age, racial, and socioeconomic demographics, hence rendering them susceptible to a range of health complications and an increased risk of premature mortality. The frequency of obesity among adolescent females in Iran has exhibited an increase from 6 to 9%, while among boys, it has risen from 2 to 7%.

pmc-11692407.title: THE USE OF MINDFULNESS-BASED INTERVENTION FOR LONG-TERM CARE RESIDENTS: A REVIEW OF THE LITERATURE
pmc-11692407.creator: Audrieanna Raciti, Yu-Ping Chang
pmc-11692407.description: Physiological and psychological health is a significant concern among people residing in long term care. Researchers have begun to design and test mindfulness-based interventions (MBIs) as a strategy to lessen the burden of these impacts on long-term care residents as well as our already strained healthcare system.

pmc-11714002.title: Potentially modifiable risk factors for dementia putting the evidence together: Total population attributable fraction
pmc-11714002.creator: Gill Livingston, Jonathan D Huntley, Kathy Y Liu, Sergi Costafreda Gonzalez, Geir Selbaek, Suvarna Alladi, David Ames, Sube Banerjee, Alistair Burns, Carol Brayne, Nick C Fox, Cleusa P Ferri, Laura N Gitlin, Robert J Howard, Helen C Kales, Mika Kivimaki, Eric B Larson, Noeline Nakasujja, Kenneth Roc
pmc-11714002.description: BackgroundOur authors from around the world met to summarise the available knowledge, decide which potentially modifiable risk factors for dementia have compelling evidence and create the most comprehensive analysis to date for potentially modifiable risk factors to inform policy, give individuals the opportunity to control their risks and generate research.

pmc-12437076.title: Effectiveness and efficiency of Virtual Reality cognitive behavioural therapy for paranoid delusions - results from a randomized clinical trial
pmc-12437076.creator: W Veling
pmc-12437076.description: Abstract: BackgroundCognitive behaviour therapy is the main evidence-based psychological treatment for paranoid ideations in patients with psychotic disorders. Virtual reality may improve psychological treatment, because it facilitates behaviour interventions aimed at reducing avoidance and dropping safety behaviours. We investigated the effects of virtual-reality-based cognitive behaviour therapy for paranoid ideations (VR-CBTp) compared to standard CBTp.

pmc-12591880.title: Precision stratified treatment of primary hyperparathyroidism based on multilevel emerging biomarkers
pmc-12591880.creator: Xi Zhu, Qi Zhang, Linghui Wang, Shuting Xu, Enmei Gong, Bin Zhou, Yong Wu, Zhouting Li, Yanjie Zhao, Shuhui Li, Feng Cheng, Lei Zhu
pmc-12591880.description: Primary hyperparathyroidism (PHPT) is a clinically heterogeneous endocrine disorder whose management has historically been guided by biochemical profiles and symptomatic presentation. However, the limitations of conventional diagnostic and therapeutic strategies—including poor sensitivity in detecting subclinical organ damage and an inability to predict disease progression—have underscored the need for a more nuanced, biomarker-driven approach.

pmc-12653722.title: Xyloglucan Endotransglycosylase/Hydrolase Downregulation Increases Nicotiana benthamiana Tolerance to Tobacco Mosaic Virus Infection
pmc-12653722.creator: Natalia M. Ershova, Ekaterina V. Sheshukova, Kamila A. Kamarova, Alfiya R. Alimova, Yana Y. Savchenko, Alexandra A. Antimonova, Tatiana V. Komarova
pmc-12653722.description: The biological functions of the multiple members of the xyloglucan endotransglycosylase/hydrolase (XTH) protein family are rather diverse: XTHs are cell wall remodeling enzymes that participate in plant growth and development, are involved in responses to various environmental stresses and interactions with pathogenic and symbiotic microorganisms. However, XTHs’ role upon viral infection remains poorly understood.

pmc-12656448.title: Recent Developments and Challenges of Edge Termination Techniques for Vertical Diamond Schottky Barrier Diodes
pmc-12656448.creator: Genzhuang Li, Wang Lin, Shishuai Liu, Yeldos Aileplanm, Aochen Du, Liuan Li, Antonio Di Bartolomeo
pmc-12656448.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Thanks to its excellent material properties, diamond-based power electronic devices have garnered widespread attention. The realization of large-sized (over 2 inches) and high-quality single-crystal diamond wafers has significantly accelerated the industrialization of diamond semiconductor materials and devices. Over years of development, diamond Schottky barrier diodes (SBDs) have evolved into three primary device structures: lateral conduction type, quasi-vertical conduction type, and vertical conduction type. However, the performance of these devices has yet to fully unlock the potential of diamond materials.

pmc-12949243.title: Microbially produced bile acids are associated with increased IgG autoantibodies and poorer mental wellbeing in fibromyalgia
pmc-12949243.creator: Jenny E. Jakobsson, Henrik Carlsson, Ida Erngren, Joana Menezes, Emerson Krock, Matthew A. Hunt, Jeanette Tour Sohlin, Asma Al-Grety, Katalin Sandor, Eva Kosek, Camilla I. Svensson, Kim Kultima
pmc-12949243.description: Fibromyalgia (FM) is a disease primarily associated with chronic widespread pain, but other common symptoms are anxiety and depression. We previously proposed that autoimmunity contributes to FM based on findings of increased immunoglobulin G binding to satellite glial cells (anti-SGC IgG) in FM subjects compared to healthy controls (HC).

pmc-13050364.title: Risk of Depression, Anxiety, and Suicidal Behavior in Older Adults With Severe Vision Loss
pmc-13050364.creator: Charles Zhang, Georges AbouKasm, Jonathan B Lin, Kisha Kalra, Joaquín Sosa Lockward, Audina Berrocal
pmc-13050364.description: Purpose: To evaluate the risk of developing depression, anxiety, and suicidal behavior in older adults newly diagnosed with blindness. Methods: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using the TriNetX Analytics Network, analyzing de-identified electronic health records from 2006 to 2024.

pmc-13150785.title: How does stochasticity in learning impact the accumulation of knowledge and the evolution of learning?
pmc-13150785.creator: Ludovic Maisonneuve, Laurent Lehmann
pmc-13150785.description: Learning is crucial for humans and other animals to acquire knowledge, enhancing survival and reproduction. In particular, individual and social learning allow populations to accumulate knowledge across generations. Here, we examine how stochasticity in the production and social acquisition of knowledge influences the evolution of learning schedules and cumulative knowledge.

pmc-13323806.title: Barriers to Optimization of Medical Therapy and the Role of Checklist‐Based Decision Support in Heart Failure
pmc-13323806.creator: Brett M. Montelaro, Edward Woods, Candace D. Speight, Eisha P. Udeshi, Andrea R. Mitchell, Michael A. Burke, Jamie Diamond, Alanna A. Morris, Engels N. Obi, Andra S. Stevenson, Molly Tiedeken, Neal W. Dickert
pmc-13323806.description: BackgroundGuideline‐directed medical therapy (GDMT) reduces morbidity and mortality in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, yet it remains underused. Patient‐activation interventions, including checklist‐based decision support, have shown improvement in GDMT optimization, and iterative refinement of such tools may enhance their impact.

pmc-13326377.title: Broadly neutralizing antibodies for HIV therapy in clinical trials: a systematic review
pmc-13326377.creator: Jinfang Zhao, Hui Wu, Jiayi He, Yinsong Luo, Jiaye Liu
pmc-13326377.description: BackgroundLifelong daily antiretroviral therapy (ART) effectively suppresses human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1) replication but does not eradicate the virus, underscoring the urgent need for long-acting antivirals and functional cure strategies. Broadly neutralizing antibodies (bNAbs) have emerged as a promising approach for achieving durable HIV-1 remission.

pmc-13341415.title: The relationship between athletic identity and kinesiophobia in young athletes with prior sport-related injury

pmc-13416652.title: Oral vitamin D3 supplementation enhances antiviral immunity in chickens challenged with fowl adenovirus serotype 4
pmc-13416652.creator: Zhanbang Ma, Fangfang Wang, Bing Wang, Zhihui Zuo, Zongxi Han, Huixin Li, Deying Ma
pmc-13416652.description: Vitamin D is increasingly recognized as an important regulator of innate and adaptive immunity, yet its antiviral role in chickens during fowl adenovirus serotype 4 (FAdV-4) infection remains unclear. In this study, we investigated the effects of oral vitamin D3 supplementation on humoral immunity, tissue viral load, and immune-related gene expression in FAdV-4-infected chickens.

pmc-13417040.title: Polygonatum kiangnanense (Asparagaceae), a new species from southeastern China

pmc-13523875.creator: Wei Zhang, Dandan Yang, Rong Shao, Tiantian Lai, Xiuqin Feng
pmc-13523875.description: In the first-in-human (FIH) study, the intravenous (IV) administration represents a critical juncture where preclinical data meet human physiology, characterized by immediate systemic exposure and an extremely narrow margin for safety. The current management measures for these trials are fragmented and lack a systematic framework.

pmc-13571630.title: Vision Restoration to People with Long-Term Blindness Using the Brain-Computer Interface Technology: A Sociotechnical Research Framework to Improve Usefulness for Users
pmc-13571630.creator: Zdenek Smutny, Milan Hudec, Ines Kožuh
pmc-13571630.description: Invasive and non-invasive brain-computer interface (BCI) represent a promising technology for treating various diseases and disabilities. BCI-based invasive solutions also include visual prostheses. Currently, there is rapid development of cortical prostheses and bold statements, eg, about the potential of Neuralink’s experimental neuroprosthetic Blindsight to restore vision.
